title: Session: an adult's childhood abuse, and the children he lives with now

objective: Report suspected child abuse or neglect as a mandated reporter, on time and to the right agency
secondaryObjectives: Explain confidentiality with minors, guardians and multiple parties under Washington law
Explain the protections for people who report in good faith, including whistleblowers

sources.cite: RCW 26.44.030 (last amended 2025 c 197 s 2 and 2025 c 192 s 2): (1)(a) psychologists are mandated reporters; a report goes 'to the proper law enforcement agency or to the department'; (1)(h) 'at the first opportunity, but in no case longer than 48 hours'; (2) the duty does not cover abuse in childhood discovered after the person is an adult, unless 'there is reasonable cause to believe other children are or may be at risk of abuse or neglect by the accused'

brief.situation: You are a licensed psychologist in outpatient practice in Washington. Jenna Marsh, 27 (a fictional client), has seen you for three months for depression. Today she sits down and says there is something she has never told anyone. You have 50 minutes.
handover: Depression, moderate, improving with weekly therapy; works at a veterinary clinic; close to her older sister, Kelsey, who has two children.
At intake you explained the limits of confidentiality in writing, including mandated reports of child abuse.
howItWorks: Choose what to say and do from the action groups. Jenna answers at once; then let the conversation continue, which moves the session clock by the minutes that exchange took.
Her rapport, distress and how much she discloses change with what you say. What she tells you depends on the trust you have built.
The hour ends at 50 minutes. After the session you write a short formulation and document.

source.cite: Common outpatient practice: a 50-minute session (the 'therapy hour')
source.note: Author's scenario timing; the session can be ended earlier.
How rapport and distress move with each response is a teaching simplification for exam practice, not a validated model of a client.

checkIn.label: Open-ended check-in: 'Take your time. What's on your mind?'

effects.log: You ask an open question and give the client room to answer.

effects.finding: She is quiet for a long moment. "There's something I've never said out loud. I don't know if I can."

reflect.label: Reflect what you hear (empathic reflection)
reflect.why: You have reflected a lot already; move the session on.

effects.log: You reflect the feeling under what was said, without judging it.

effects.finding: Jenna nods slowly. "It's been sitting on me for years."

invitePast.label: Invite her to share what she wants to, at her own pace, and only as much as she chooses

effects.log: You tell her she can go at her own pace and share only what she chooses.

then.finding: "When I was eight to twelve I spent summers with my uncle Ray. He hurt me. Physically, a lot. Nobody knew. I never told anyone."
"Never mind. It's stupid. Forget it." (She is not ready yet.)

validate.label: Believe her and acknowledge how hard that was to say, without pressing for details
validate.available: not talking and (pastDisclosed and not validated)

effects.log: You tell her you believe her, that it took courage to say, and that she does not have to say more than she wants to.

effects.finding: She lets out a breath. "I thought you'd ask me a hundred questions."

pressDetails.label: Ask her to describe exactly what he did to her
pressDetails.available: not talking and (pastDisclosed and not pressedDetails)

effects.log: You ask for the details of what her uncle did.

effects.finding: She goes still and stares at the floor. "I can't. I don't want to."

effects.log: Pressing for details she has not offered can retraumatize her, and nothing you must decide today depends on them.

askAround.label: Ask, gently, whether Ray is around children now
askAround.available: not talking and (pastDisclosed and not kidsKnown)
askAround.why: Asked (or she has not told you about him yet).

effects.log: You ask whether her uncle has contact with any children today.

effects.finding: "That's why I'm telling you now. Last month he moved in with Kelsey and her kids. Ava's nine, Mason's six. Ava told me on the phone, 'Uncle Ray gets scary.'"

effects.log: Her own childhood abuse need not be reported now that she is an adult, but there is reasonable cause to believe Ava and Mason may be at risk from the same man (RCW 26.44.030(2)).

tellDuty.label: Tell her honestly: because Ava and Mason may be at risk, you are required to report, what you will say, and that what she does about her own history stays her choice
tellDuty.available: not talking and (kidsKnown and not toldHer)
tellDuty.why: Said (or you do not yet know about the children).

effects.log: You explain plainly that the law requires you to report because her niece and nephew may be at risk, what the report will say, and that her own history remains hers to decide about.

then.finding: She cries. "Kelsey's going to be so angry." Then, quietly: "Okay. I wanted someone to do something. I just couldn't be the one."
"I told you because I trusted you."

callNow.label: Call the child abuse intake line now, with her there: Ray's name and address, the children, what Ava said, and Jenna's own history with him
callNow.available: not talking and (kidsKnown and not reported)
callNow.why: Reported (or you do not yet know about the children).

effects.log: You call the state's child abuse intake line and report Ray's name, where he lives, the two children, what Ava said, and that he physically abused Jenna as a child.

effects.finding: Intake takes the report and asks how to reach Kelsey's home. Jenna listens, holding the cushion.

effects.log: Reported at the first opportunity, well inside 48 hours, to the department's intake (RCW 26.44.030).

callSister.label: Call her sister Kelsey first to ask whether the kids are all right
callSister.available: not talking and (kidsKnown and not investigated)

effects.log: You call Kelsey and ask how the children are doing with Ray in the house.

effects.finding: Kelsey is cold: "Why are you asking? Did Jenna say something?" Ray's voice is in the background.

effects.log: Checking is the investigators' job. Calling the household can tip off the accused, and you shared Jenna's information without her consent.

promise.label: Promise her nothing she said today will leave this room
promise.available: not talking and (pastDisclosed and not promised)

effects.log: You promise her that what she said stays here.
A promise you cannot keep: children may be at risk, and the report is not optional.

askPermission.label: Ask her whether she wants you to make a report
askPermission.available: not talking and (pastDisclosed and not askedPermission and not reported)

effects.log: You ask Jenna whether she wants you to report.

effects.finding: "No. Please. Kelsey will never speak to me again."

effects.log: When children may be at risk, the report is not hers to permit or refuse (RCW 26.44.030).

pressPolice.label: Tell her she has to report what Ray did to her to the police
pressPolice.available: not talking and (pastDisclosed and not pressured)

effects.log: You tell Jenna she must go to the police about her own abuse.

effects.finding: "I'm not ready for that. You're not listening."

effects.log: She is an adult; what to do about her own abuse is her decision. Offer options, not orders.

minimize.label: Tell her it was a long time ago and the focus should be on the present
minimize.available: not talking and (pastDisclosed and not minimized)

effects.log: You suggest it was long ago and she should focus on now.

effects.finding: She pulls the cushion closer and says nothing.

offerOptions.label: Tell her about her own options, at her pace: a victim advocate, a police report if and when she chooses, and working on this in therapy
offerOptions.available: not talking and (pastDisclosed and not optionsOffered)

effects.log: You describe her own options without steering: an advocate, a police report only if and when she wants one, and continuing this work in therapy.

effects.finding: "Maybe the advocate. Not the police. Not yet."

tonightPlan.label: Plan the rest of today with her: grounding before she leaves, who she will be with tonight, and a session this week
tonightPlan.available: not talking and (pastDisclosed and not tonightPlan)

effects.log: You plan the hours ahead with her: a grounding exercise now, her roommate tonight, and a session on Thursday.
You close the session.

options.label: Call intake now, before you leave today
Wait until next week's session to learn more first
No report: she is an adult and asked you not to

then.log: Reported after the session, the same day.
Put off to next week: past the 48 hours the statute allows.

document.label: Document the session and the report

options.label: What she said in her words, what Ava said, the report (time, intake, what was reported), and the plan
Uncle abused client as a child and is probably abusing the niece

effects.log: Documented: note {recordDoc}.

effects.log: The 50-minute hour is up. The session ends here.
Jenna stands, says she should never have said anything, and leaves before the hour is over.

adult.title: Predict (not scored)
adult.context: Jenna is 27; the abuse she describes happened when she was a child. Before you respond: does what she has said so far require a report?

choices.label: Not on its own; it depends on whether other children may be at risk from him now

effects.log: Prediction: depends on other children.

choices.feedback: Right. RCW 26.44.030(2) does not require a report of childhood abuse discovered after the person is an adult, unless there is reasonable cause to believe other children are or may be at risk from the accused. That is the question to ask next.

choices.label: Yes: any abuse a client discloses must be reported

effects.log: Prediction: always report.

choices.feedback: Not in Washington. An adult's own childhood abuse is excluded unless other children are or may be at risk from the accused (RCW 26.44.030(2)). Reporting it anyway would disclose her information without a legal basis.

choices.label: No: she is an adult, so there is nothing to report

effects.log: Prediction: never.

choices.feedback: Too fast. The exclusion has an exception: if other children are or may be at risk from the same person, the duty applies (RCW 26.44.030(2)). Ask about children now.

formulation.question: Write your formulation: why her own history did not by itself require a report, why you reported, and how you supported her.

parts.label: The duty
parts.criteria: Childhood abuse discovered after the person is an adult is excluded unless other children are or may be at risk from the accused (RCW 26.44.030(2)); Ray lives with two children and Ava's words give reasonable cause; a psychologist reports at the first opportunity and within 48 hours, to the department or law enforcement; report, do not investigate or ask permission.
parts.modelAnswer: Jenna's own abuse, disclosed now that she is 27, would not by itself require a report (RCW 26.44.030(2)). But Ray now lives with her niece and nephew, and Ava has said he 'gets scary': reasonable cause to believe they may be at risk from him. As a psychologist I am a mandated reporter, so I called the department's intake during the session, well within 48 hours. I did not call her sister to check; that is the investigators' job.

parts.label: Supporting her
parts.criteria: Believed her without pressing for details; told her before reporting, honestly, without promises; her own history left to her, with options (an advocate, police if and when she chooses); a plan for tonight and a session this week; a factual note.
parts.modelAnswer: I believed her and did not ask for details. I told her before I called why I had to report and what I would say, and promised nothing I could not keep. What she does about her own abuse is her choice; I offered an advocate and said a police report is hers to make if and when she wants. We planned tonight with her roommate and a session Thursday. My note records her words, Ava's words and the report, not conclusions.

expertPath.text: Check in and reflect; invite her to share at her pace; believe her without pressing for details.
Ask whether Ray is around children now: he lives with her niece and nephew.
Tell her why you must report and what you will say; call intake with her there.
Offer her own options (an advocate; police only if and when she chooses); plan tonight and Thursday; a factual note.

reportedSupported.headline: Good: reported, and she was heard
reportedSupported.body: You knew why her own history alone did not require a report and why the children did (RCW 26.44.030(2)), reported at the first opportunity, told her first, and left her own choices with her.

gaps.headline: Reported, with gaps
gaps.body: The children are reported; the criteria below show what was late or missing.

reportedLost.headline: Reported, at the cost of her trust
reportedLost.body: Telling her before you call, without promises, is what keeps a client who has just disclosed abuse in therapy (APA 4.02).

notReported.headline: No report
notReported.body: An adult's childhood abuse is excluded only until there is reasonable cause to believe other children are or may be at risk from the accused; then a psychologist reports at the first opportunity and within 48 hours (RCW 26.44.030). Her permission is not required.

tippedOff.headline: Tipped off
tippedOff.body: Calling the household warns the accused and discloses her information. Report, and let the department investigate.

walkout.headline: She left
walkout.body: Pressing for details, pushing her to the police, or brushing it off drives a client out of the room right after the hardest thing she has said.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: Nothing was documented before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Jenna's own abuse, disclosed as an adult, does not by itself trigger a report: RCW 26.44.030(2) excludes childhood abuse discovered after the person is an adult unless there is reasonable cause to believe other children are or may be at risk from the accused. So ask about children now: Ray lives with her niece and nephew, and Ava says he 'gets scary'. That is reasonable cause, and a psychologist reports to the department or law enforcement at the first opportunity and within 48 hours. Report; do not call the family to check or ask her permission. Tell her first, honestly and without promises; leave what she does about her own abuse to her, with options; plan tonight; document facts, not conclusions.
